conversion: The one bundled file is decoded to mono 44100 Hz signed 16-bit PCM WAV; no content processing is applied to it. Slowing, de-flickering, filtering, looping, and every synthesized bubble happen at render time in engine.py so the bundled file stays comparable to what the source page serves.
verification: The fireplace bed's licence was read from its own source page (not a search result, not a mirror). It is bundled here by copy from the sibling fire_sound_generator, which sourced the same file first; the original download's SHA-256 recorded there is carried over, and the decoded copy's own SHA-256 is recorded as bundled_sha256.
hybrid_note: Lava is a hybrid. The recorded half is the roar bed below; the synthesized half is the bubbles, which are not recorded at all. A bubble surfacing has a rate, and a rate is not a period -- so the bubbles are procedural (resonant exp-decay tones, gliding down, with a wet noise burst) and only the chaotic aperiodic roar is a recording. That split is why only one file is bundled.

excluded.name: 25 CC0 mud sfx (rubberduck)
excluded.reason: The obvious recording to reach for: thick mud bubbles bursting, slowed, is the classic lava-bubble Foley, and it is CC0 (noted so by fire_sound_generator's README, which scoped lava before this generator existed). Not bundled, and not for a licensing reason -- the bubbles here are synthesized. A bubble is a clean resonant transient with a rate, which is exactly what procedural DSP does well, so no bubble recording is bundled at all. Reach for this first if a recorded-bubble variant is ever wanted.

excluded.name: environment_ambience_generator's procedural lava loop
excluded.reason: Not a licensing exclusion. That package had a fully-synthesized lava loop -- roar and all -- and it was removed alongside its fire on 2026-07-15. The roar is the part synthesis lost on (chaotic, broadband, correlated across frequency in ways filtered noise is not), which is why the roar here is a recording. Kept in the record so nobody re-derives a lava roar from oscillators and wonders why it was not done that way.

collections.name: Fireplace Sound loop
collections.author: PagDev
collections.borrowed_from: fire_sound_generator/sources/pagdev_fireplace.wav (same CC0 origin; copied so lava is self-contained)
collections.note: 29 s of wood burning -- fire's burning bed, which at its lowest scale is most of what lava is: a slow viscous roar. Every sustained cue and the roar under every event is built from it, slowed and de-flickered into molten rock.
